title: AltDigital Managed Platform — onboarding questionnaire
description: Structured form of design/onboarding-questionnaire.md, which is the INPUT to account vesting rather than a document that gets filed. Only [A] asked fields appear here. [D] derived fields are computed by scripts/derive-vesting.py from vesting/derivation-rules.yaml and are rejected if supplied, because a derived value that can be typed is a derived value that can be wrong. [P] placeholder fields are owned outside this process and are marked required-but-nullable so their absence is visible rather than assumed.

schema_version.description: Pinned. A questionnaire is an audit artifact re-reviewed on the triggers listed in the source document, so a record written today must still be readable when its schema has moved on.

partner.description: 1.0 — partner slug. Must already exist and be active in the registry; create-client-ou.sh blocks otherwise. 18 chars to fit the account alias budget.

client_slug.description: 1.1 — machine-safe client id used in account alias and root email.

application_code.description: 1.3 — 10 chars. Tighter than client because the email local part is capped at 64 octets by RFC 5321, which binds before the 63-char account alias.

service_model.description: 1.4 — drives patching ownership, SLA scope, DNS and certificate ownership.

partner_is_application_owner.description: 1.0b — if true the partner appears in two columns of the responsibility matrix, which needs saying out loud rather than inferring.

breach_notification_contact.description: Who AltDigital notifies of a breach affecting this application: the notification of record that starts the client's own clock. Design 07: AltDigital notifies the PARTNER, never the partner's client, so for a partner-mediated client this is the partner's contact; for a 'direct' client, or where the partner owns the application, it is the client's. Must be a person who can act for the organisation legally -- not a consultant holding that organisation's email address. Required since 2026-10-01: the first real questionnaire named a security contact who was an AltDigital partner acting for the client, which would have had AltDigital notifying itself.

security_contact.description: Day-to-day security operations contact: findings, questions, 'is this activity yours?'. Distinct from breach_notification_contact, and may be a delegate. Optional; absent, security questions go to the technical contact.

frameworks.description: 2.1 — drives conformance packs, retention floor and pen test cadence. 'none' must be alone; enforced in derive-vesting.py, since JSON Schema cannot express 'this value excludes all others' without oneOf gymnastics that obscure the rule. 'hitrust' (HITRUST CSF) added 2026-09-30 so it is asked every time: health plans commonly require it of vendors, and it was nearly missed on the first real questionnaire. No conformance pack is mapped to it; derive-vesting.py warns.

non_us_data_subjects.description: 2.2 — asks about DATA SUBJECTS, not customer location. True HALTS vesting: region choice then carries a residency and transfer position that is a legal determination, and the platform's allowed regions are US-only.

data_classification.description: 2.3 — seeds the egress profile default and monitoring tier.

baa_window_partner_to_client_hours.description: 2.6 — marked [P] in the source: owned by Art and Wayne, not asked of the customer here. Nullable so an unanswered value is VISIBLE. Null blocks vesting where PHI is true; a missing key would let it pass unnoticed, which is the failure this nullability exists to prevent. AltDigital's own window (2.6a) is not here at all — it comes from the partner's registry record and must be strictly tighter.

egress_profile.description: 3.2 — the customer's answer overrides the classification-derived default. 'locked' is accepted here but NOT implemented (B-010); derive-vesting.py flags it rather than failing at the network step after three accounts exist.

inbound_cross_tenant_api.description: 3.4 — true is documented as an arm's-length public API. No private connectivity is provisioned between tenants, ever.

outbound_allowlist.description: 3.5 — domains for the Network Firewall or DNS Firewall rule set.

uat_required.description: 3a.1 — opt-in fourth account. Raises AWS cost.

release_cadence.description: 3a.2 — drives HOOP versus seasonal teardown. Required when uat_required is true; enforced in derive-vesting.py.

usage_pattern.description: 3a.3 — seasonal makes the account eligible for the dormant lifecycle.

timezone.description: 3a.7, client form 5.2 — the DEFAULT timezone for every schedule that does not name its own. Schedules may each carry their own (a HOOP in the developers' zone, a production window in the users'), because asking a partner to convert between zones is how 'IST' and a window that crosses midnight arrived on the first real questionnaire.

uat.description: 3a.6 — saving here is modest; users test on their own schedule.

manual_turnup_authorised.description: 3a.8 — who may bring an environment up outside its HOOP. Empty means nobody can, which is a support call waiting to happen.

rpo_hours.description: 4.2 — default 2. Drives backup frequency and PITR.

backup_retention_days.description: 4.4 — how long backup COPIES are kept in the cross-account vault, in days. null means the platform default of 35. The floor is 35 and is not a preference: the copy vault is under Vault Lock with MinRetentionDays 35, and a copy job specifying less is rejected outright — one failure per resource per schedule, indefinitely, reported per job so it reads as a resource problem. Raising this is a client conversation; lowering it is not available while the lock stands, and after the lock hardens it is not available at all. This is NOT the local vault's retention, which follows the tier (config/tiers.yaml `backup_policy`) and is a cost decision rather than a commitment. Local retention governs how fast a restore can be; this governs how far back one can reach.

maintenance_windows.description: 4.5, client form 5.6 / 5.7. Two windows because they optimise for different people: production's avoids the application's USERS, non-production's avoids the DEVELOPERS. Each may carry its own timezone, defaulting to environments.timezone.

prod.description: 5.6 — production is always on, so no HOOP check applies. May cross midnight.

nonprod.description: 5.7 — dev, test and uat. Either a choice, from which derive-vesting.py computes a window per scheduled environment using vesting/derivation-rules.yaml, or a window the client specifies. 'outside-developer-hours' is the form's recommended answer: it is the one a partner who is not a developer can answer correctly. A window outside a scheduled environment's HOOP means the environment must be woken for it (B-141, not built); derive-vesting.py reports that as a warning.

external_key_material.description: 5.3 — BYOK. Creates an EXTERNAL-origin key, which AWS cannot rotate and cannot recover if the customer loses the material.

no_regulated_data_in_lower_envs_ack.description: 5.7 — must be TRUE. Modelled as a const rather than a boolean because a questionnaire that records 'customer declined to acknowledge' and proceeds anyway is worse than one that cannot be submitted. If a customer will not acknowledge it, that is a scope conversation, not a field value.

developer_manager_role.description: 3.6a -- does the development manager also write and deploy code, or oversee only? Either way they receive TenantReadOnly in every environment. 'contributor' additionally requires them on the developer roster with the environments they build in; 'oversight' forbids it, so that an oversight-only answer cannot quietly acquire build access through the roster. Enforced by scripts/derive-roster.py. Required, with no default: the two answers grant different things, and a default would decide that for the client.

dedicated_infrastructure_required.description: 5.9 — SECURITY-motivated, distinct from section 6 which is about LICENCES. Default false; docs/isolation-tiers.md carries the argument. Conflating the two produces a client paying a tenancy premium nobody can later explain.

dedicated_infrastructure_driver.description: 5.9a — determines whether it is negotiable. Required when 5.9 is true.

dedicated_infrastructure_control_ref.description: 5.9b — if a framework is cited, which control. Frameworks are cited far more often than read; none of HIPAA, PCI-DSS or SOC 2 requires dedicated physical hardware.

working_definition.description: 7.1 — 'what would a user notice first if it broke?' The source document calls this the only question a customer can genuinely fail to answer well, and it drives BOTH the canary and the SLA measurement. minLength is a blunt instrument against a one-word answer; it cannot detect a useless twenty-character one, and this remains a conversation rather than a form field.

acceptable_response_ms.description: 7.4 — canary timeout AND the SLA pass condition. One number, two consumers, deliberately.

existing_test_suite.description: 7.5 — decides Fargate canary runner versus native Synthetics.

cicd_tooling.description: 8.1 — OIDC federation for the AppDeployer role.

ticketing.description: Client form 12.4. Where this application's change records live, which is where change reconciliation (design 08) looks for the approval covering each deployment. Replaced change.jira_change_project on 2026-10-01, when the first tenant kept its records on its own Atlassian site. 'none' is allowed and means application deployments are reported UNAVAILABLE, never as approved or unapproved; derive-vesting.py says so.

system.description: altdigital-jira: a project on AltDigital's Jira. client-jira: the client's own Atlassian site, read by a read-only service account the client creates there, stored with scripts/set-jira-token.sh --tenant. none: change records are kept elsewhere or not at all.

product.description: Jira Service Management records carry approval decisions with the approvers' identities, which is what lets reconciliation check WHO approved. Jira Software has no approval records; reconciliation falls back to the status name. Required unless system is none.

site.description: The client's Atlassian site. Required for client-jira, refused otherwise.

project_key.description: The Jira project holding this application's change records. Required unless system is none.

work_spaces.description: Client form 12.7. Spaces (Jira projects) to create on AltDigital's Jira for the team's own work, separate from where change records live (12.4). Arc8 kept change records on its own site and still wanted a Scrum board on ours, so this does not depend on 12.4. Omitted or empty means none. Members are named by roster ROLE, never by person, so the questionnaire stays free of personal data and a space's membership follows the roster. Creation is by hand today; derive-vesting.py lists what to create.

key.description: Jira project key. Unique across the list, and not the 12.4c change-record project when that is on AltDigital's Jira.

template.description: scrum: sprints, backlog and a sprint board (Jira Software). kanban: a continuous-flow board, no sprints (Jira Software). service-management: a request queue (Jira Service Management).

members.description: Roster roles added to the space: developers (3b developers) and/or readonly (the development manager and other read-only oversight).

ip_boundary_ack.description: 9.1 — const for the same reason as 5.7.

post_exit_governance_loss_ack.description: 9.2 — the customer loses platform governance on exit. Acknowledged before vesting, not discovered at exit.

evidence.description: Section 17 — where the client's APPLICATION-layer evidence goes (D-029, decided 2026-10-04). Infrastructure evidence (platform-built resources, AltDigital's own actions, account-level findings) goes to AltDigital's Truveon tenant regardless and is not asked about. Required with no 'none' value, so 'this client has no destination' is a form error rather than a state the pipeline has to handle. Cross-field rules are enforced in scripts/derive-vesting.py check_evidence.

destination.description: 17.1 — truveon: the client's Truveon tenant (section 16 required), which they may also use for their own governance. external: the client's own compliance platform; a connector is built per vendor when first needed. archive: neither; evidence goes to a low-cost bucket, kept 18 months, then expired. Only truveon is vestable until B-157 phase D builds the archive.

external_platform.description: 17.2 — the client's compliance platform by product name (e.g. Vanta, Drata). Required when destination is external.

exposure_acceptance.description: 17.3 — required when the client declares regulatory exposure (any framework other than 'none', phi, or cardholder_data) and chooses archive. Not a gap: a dated, owned record that the client knows its obligations and chose not to address them through AltDigital. A role, not a name; the signed document is where the person is.

accepted_on.description: Date of the client's written acceptance.

accepted_by_role.description: The accepting officer's role, e.g. 'CEO'. Not a name.

reference.description: Where the signed acceptance is kept: a document id, not the document.

truveon.description: Section 16 — the client's Truveon tenant. One tenant per CLIENT, not per application (B-023, decided 2026-09-23); a second application for the same client reuses the tenant and adds itself as an application inside it. Optional in the schema so questionnaires completed before this section existed still validate; scripts/truveon-tenant-handoff.sh refuses to prepare a tenant without it. Holds no personal data: the people who get Truveon accounts are in the Truveon roster sidecar, vesting/truveon.roster.example.yaml.

existing_tenant.description: 16.1 — true if the client already has a Truveon tenant (a Truveon customer before they were a platform tenant, or a second application for an onboarded client). Creation is skipped; the tenant is configured and linked only.

tenant_slug.description: 16.2 — Truveon tenant slug. It becomes a Postgres schema name in Truveon and cannot be changed afterwards without a migration. Defaults to identity.client_slug. Set it when two partners have clients with the same slug, since Truveon slugs are global and platform client slugs are unique only within a partner.

tenant_name.description: 16.2 — display name in Truveon. Defaults to identity.client_name.

legal_entities.description: 16.3 — the client's legal structure, for Truveon's entity model. Optional: Truveon creates a root 'Group' entity regardless and entries without parent_ref attach beneath it. Company facts only; signing officers are people and are entered in Truveon directly.

send_invites.description: 16.4 — email Truveon invites to the roster when the tenant is created. Default false: accounts are created silently and invited during the white-glove walkthrough, so a client does not receive a login before anybody has shown them what it is for.

contact.description: Contacts are personal data. A completed questionnaire therefore must NEVER be committed — enforced in .gitignore and the pre-commit hook, the same treatment as config/contacts.env.

timezone.description: Optional. Defaults to environments.timezone. Usually the developers' zone.

hoop.description: Hours of Planned Operation. always_on true ignores the rest; false requires days, start and end, enforced in derive-vesting.py because JSON Schema's if/then for this reads far worse than the check it replaces. A HOOP may NOT cross midnight — the scheduler cannot run one — but giving it in the developers' own timezone almost always removes the crossing.

window.description: A maintenance window, written the way people say it. An end earlier than the start crosses midnight: 23:00-01:00 is two hours ending the next morning, and `days` are the days the window STARTS. An end equal to the start is rejected, since it could mean nothing or all day.

timezone.description: An IANA timezone name, e.g. America/Denver or Asia/Kolkata. Abbreviations are rejected by the pattern: IST is India, Ireland or Israel depending on who is asked, and MT does not say whether daylight saving applies (Denver observes it, Phoenix does not). The pattern only checks shape; derive-vesting.py confirms the name resolves.
